observations: Audited all four DAO files for manual JDBC Connection lifecycle and transaction handling.

Targeted the seven primary unclosed transaction mutations: ThuCungDAO.insertThuCung, ThuCungDAO.deleteThuCung, NhanVienDAO.insertNhanVien, NhanVienDAO.updateNhanVien, NhanVienDAO.deleteNhanVien, SanPhamDAO.deleteSanPham, and LichHenDAO.deleteLichHen.
Updated each finally block so that conn.setAutoCommit(true) is guarded independently in its own try-catch, followed immediately by an independent try-catch invoking conn.close().

Checked all manual connection finally blocks across the four files: LichHenDAO.insertLichHen previously grouped conn.setAutoCommit(true) and conn.close() inside a single try block, which risked skipping close() if setAutoCommit threw; separated them into independent guards to prevent cleanup bypass.
Preserved all catch blocks, rollback invocations, and exception re-throwing without modifying public signatures or business logic.
Patch proposals use normalized LF, exact contextual substrings for unique single matching, and correct base SHA256 hashes.
output.summary: Created patch artifact docs/ai-context/patches/agy-patch-jdbc-close-20261108.json addressing connection cleanup in manual transaction DAO mutations across ThuCungDAO, NhanVienDAO, SanPhamDAO, and LichHenDAO.
